issues.t: Lower intake manifold gasket coolant leak
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle you can trace, a sweet smell, the temperature gauge creeping up, or milky brown sludge under the oil cap. Some owners see white exhaust smoke.
issues.why: The 3.4L V6 uses plastic-framed lower intake gaskets that break down over time, especially with old coolant. Coolant then leaks outside the engine or into the oil.
issues.next: Check the coolant level often and do not let the engine overheat. Have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and replace the gaskets with the updated metal-framed type. If coolant got into the oil, change the oil right away to protect the bearings.

issues.t: Overheating that damages the head gaskets
issues.sym: The temperature gauge spikes, steam comes from under the hood, or the van runs hot in traffic. After a bad overheat you may get white smoke and a rough idle.
issues.why: Usually the end result of a slow coolant leak, most often from the intake gaskets, that nobody caught in time. Running the engine hot can then blow a head gasket or warp a cylinder head.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off as soon as the gauge climbs. Do not keep driving it hot. Have the cooling system and head gaskets tested before deciding whether the repair is worth it.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: The engine revs up but the van barely speeds up, gears slip, it gets stuck in one gear, or it stops moving altogether.
issues.why: The 4T65-E four-speed automatic wears out internally on many of these vans, often between 85,000 and 190,000 miles. Old fluid and heavy loads speed it up.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and color. If it slips, do not tow or load the van until it is checked. A transmission shop can tell you whether a solenoid or a full rebuild is needed.

issues.t: Hard, harsh or erratic shifting
issues.sym: Shifts slam or feel jerky, the van bangs into Drive or Reverse on cold mornings, or shifts flare and come late. The check engine light may come on.
issues.why: GM issued several bulletins for this transmission covering worn pressure control solenoids, valve body problems and computer settings that cause harsh or erratic shifts.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked. Ask the shop about the GM bulletins for the 4T65-E; a solenoid or software fix can avoid a rebuild if caught early.

issues.t: Shudder on the 1-2 shift
issues.sym: A shake or shudder when the transmission moves from first to second gear under light or moderate throttle.
issues.why: GM traced this to the second-gear clutch pack inside the 4T65-E and released a bulletin to replace it.
issues.next: Mention the shudder and the GM bulletin for the 1-2 shift to a transmission shop. Fresh fluid may help a little, but the real fix is internal.

issues.t: Power sliding door can open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger-side power sliding door may close without fully latching, and then slide open while the van is moving.
issues.why: Weak welds in the door's unlatch actuator can let it jam, so the latch never fully catches. GM ran two recalls (01V-067 and 01V-264) to fix it.
issues.next: Have a GM dealer check your VIN for the open recall. Until it is done, keep kids buckled and check that the door is fully latched.

issues.t: Sliding door handle can trap a passenger's arm (recall)
issues.sym: A passenger holding the inside handle of the power sliding door can have their arm or wrist pushed into the seat as the door opens by motor.
issues.why: On vans with second-row bucket seats, the handle sits where the opening door can pin the passenger's arm. GM recall 04V-597 replaces the handle.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the new handle was installed. Until then, open the door with the switch or key fob rather than the inside handle.

issues.t: Power sliding door won't open, close or latch
issues.sym: The power sliding door stops partway, reverses on its own, chimes, or will not open or close at all.
issues.why: The power door's motor, cable, latch and sensors wear out. GM issued several bulletins and a satisfaction campaign for door operation.
issues.next: Try resetting the door by closing it by hand and cycling the power door switch. If it still fails, have the motor, cable and latch checked.

issues.t: Dead battery from the power sliding door
issues.sym: The battery goes dead overnight or after a few days parked.
issues.why: A GM bulletin covers battery drain on vans with power sliding doors, where the door system keeps drawing current after the van is shut off.
issues.next: Have a shop do a parasitic drain test. If the door system is the cause, the bulletin repair stops the drain.

issues.t: Steering can suddenly get hard to turn (recall)
issues.sym: The steering wheel becomes much harder to turn, as if the power steering quit.
issues.why: Retainer tabs on the steering rack's lower pinion bearing were not crimped right, so bearing balls could escape. Recall 02V-286 covers it.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Have a dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Steering shaft joint can come apart (recall)
issues.sym: Loose or vague steering, clunks through the wheel, and in the worst case loss of steering.
issues.why: Collapsed insulators can loosen a joint in the steering shaft so it could separate. GM recall 99V-071 covers it.
issues.next: Get the recall status checked by VIN. Any looseness or clunk in the steering should be inspected right away.

issues.t: Wiper linkage can rub through a brake line (recall)
issues.sym: A brake fluid leak under the windshield area, a soft brake pedal, or the brake warning light.
issues.why: The windshield wiper linkage can rub against a traction control brake line until it wears through. Recall 98V-072 adds a clip and replaces damaged lines.
issues.next: If the pedal feels soft or fluid is low, do not drive the van. Have the recall done and the brake lines checked.

issues.t: Rear seat release can injure fingers (recall)
issues.sym: Fingers can get caught in the latch mechanism when folding or removing the rear bucket or split bench seats.
issues.why: The seat latch mechanisms had no protective cover. Recall 98V-145 installs covers.
issues.next: Keep fingers clear of the seat latches and ask a dealer to install the covers if they are missing.

issues.t: Fuel tank rollover valve may leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. Some owners may notice a fuel smell.
issues.why: On long-wheelbase vans, some fuel tank rollover valves did not work, so fuel could spill in a rollover. Recall 99V-268 replaces the tank.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN. Any fuel smell should be checked right away.

issues.t: Seat belt buckles may not hold in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; the buckle looks and latches normally.
issues.why: Some TRW buckle bases were not heat treated properly and may not be strong enough in a crash. Recall 00V-228 replaces affected buckles.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the buckle date codes under recall 00V-228.

issues.t: Passenger airbag built without a part (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; the airbag light may stay normal.
issues.why: Some passenger airbags were made without a check valve pin, which could make the bag deploy harder than intended. Recall 02V-329 covers it.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN and replace the airbag if needed.

issues.t: Child seat anchors in second row may not fit (recall)
issues.sym: A child seat's lower anchor clips may not attach to the second-row anchors.
issues.why: The second-row anchor wires were thicker than the federal standard allows. Recall 01V-383 covers it.
issues.next: If a child seat will not latch to the anchors, use the seat belt to install it and ask a dealer about the recall.
issues.sevReason: Child seat anchor fit/labeling recall; not a belt failure.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can crack (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign before a crash.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator could break at a weld when it fires, throwing pieces toward the driver and leaving the bag underfilled. Recall 02V-222 inspects and replaces it.
issues.next: Have a dealer check whether the airbag module was inspected under the recall.

issues.t: Hard starting, rough idle or misfire from fuel injectors
issues.sym: Long cranking before it starts, a rough or shaky idle, a light misfire, or the check engine light.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover clogged fuel injectors and injector corrosion on the 3.4L V6.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Injector cleaning or replacing the bad injectors usually fixes it.

issues.t: ABS or traction control light on
issues.sym: The ABS and traction control lights come on, and AWD models may show an AWD disabled message.
issues.why: Wheel speed sensor faults and related wiring problems set codes; GM issued bulletins for this.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read. Normal braking still works, but anti-lock does not while the light is on.

issues.t: Gauges sweep or fuel gauge reads wrong
issues.sym: The gauges jump around or sweep on their own, warning lights flicker on, or the fuel gauge shows the wrong level.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover erratic instrument clusters and inaccurate fuel gauges; a failing fuel level sender in the tank can also cause it.
issues.next: Use the trip odometer to track fuel until it is fixed. Have the cluster and fuel sender tested to see which one is at fault.

issues.t: Ticking noise after a cold start
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping from the engine right after starting cold that fades as it warms up.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for this cold-start tick on the 3.4L V6.
issues.next: If the noise fades and the oil level is fine, it is usually harmless. Have it checked if it stays loud when warm.

issues.t: Weak heat at idle in cold weather
issues.sym: The heater blows only lukewarm air at idle or low speed when it is below freezing.
issues.why: GM bulletins describe poor cabin heat at low engine speed in cold weather on these vans.
issues.next: Make sure the coolant is full, since low coolant from an intake gasket leak causes the same thing. Then ask a shop about the GM bulletin.

issues.t: Air conditioning blows warm
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm or only slightly cool, especially in hot, humid weather.
issues.why: Leaks, a worn compressor or clutch, and bulletins for weak A/C performance on these vans.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested before recharging it, so you are not paying to refill a leak.

issues.t: Water leaks at the windshield or overhead console
issues.sym: Water drips from the overhead console or map light, or wet carpet up front after rain.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover leaks at the center of the windshield seal and the overhead console area.
issues.next: Have the windshield seal and roof area water-tested and resealed.

issues.t: Tail lights or brake lights stop working
issues.sym: One or more rear lights go out even with new bulbs, or the lights flicker.
issues.why: The plastic socket plate that holds the rear bulbs melts or loses contact over time.
issues.next: Replace the socket plate, not just the bulb, since working brake lights matter for safety.

issues.t: Rust on the body and underside
issues.sym: Rust bubbles on the body, rocker panels or wheel arches, and rusty parts underneath.
issues.why: Age and road salt; owners report heavy rust on these vans at higher mileage.
issues.next: Wash the underside in winter and have brake and fuel lines checked for rust at each service.
